text.title: plan.md Structure Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules for the per-feature plan.md: exactly two H2 sections, what each must contain, when to skip the file entirely, the bias toward writing it, and the ban on splitting design and execution plan back into two files. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: plan.md has exactly two top-level sections: `## Design` and `## Execution Plan`. Both are mandatory when the feature warrants plan.md at all.
rule.rationale: Per-feature plan.md merges what used to be design.md and implementation-plan.md into ONE file; any decision change touches one file, so updates are atomic.

rule.statement: The `## Design` section MUST cover: package layout for this feature, API contracts that are FEATURE-scoped (not in project-spec), data schemas, sequencing constraints.
rule.rationale: System-wide contracts live in project-spec/. Feature-scoped contracts that exist only for this slice live here so they do not pollute the spec until they survive.

rule.statement: The `## Execution Plan` section MUST contain: wave map, task table with IDs, dependency graph, risk register.
rule.rationale: The plan is what gets executed; without IDs and dependencies the executor cannot parallelise or resume.

rule.statement: SKIP plan.md when the feature has ≤3 tasks AND introduces no new contract.
rule.rationale: For tiny features the plan.md overhead exceeds the value. The spec.md task list is structure enough.

rule.statement: If you cannot answer "is this trivial?" in one sentence, the answer is no — write plan.md.
rule.rationale: The bias should tilt toward writing the plan. The cost of one extra plan.md is low; the cost of an unplanned mid-size feature is high.

rule.statement: Two-file design + impl-plan is forbidden going forward. Single plan.md only.
rule.rationale: Atomic update beats two-file sync every time. The merge removes a recurring failure point: in F021, F022 and F002 the two files cross-referenced each other on every section and drifted whenever one was updated alone.

rule.statement: If plan.md grows long, split internally by sub-section, never by file.
rule.rationale: Length is not the failure mode — drift between the two is.

rule.statement: Cross-references between Design and Execution Plan are markdown anchors within plan.md, not cross-file links.
rule.rationale: The merge keeps the DESIGN and EXECUTION PLAN content and drops the cross-file linking discipline that nobody actually followed, together with separate file headers, separate frontmatter and separate version numbers.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit a plan.md passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the feature warrants a plan.

rule.statement: Skip; the work is a documentation-only feature, or a CR / BUG in the wrong lifecycle — use cr-bug-tracking.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the artefact is not a feature plan at all.
